**The train is all there when you come back**

**Dimensional carriages are built from the right blocks all the way through**

A dimensional carriage in the Nether stretch could come out in the wrong wood — warped on the way in, oak further along — and the extra ways out of an endless room could show the editor's stage blocks instead of real ones. ### 0.922.0

**Mining and fighting on the train no longer lag behind you**

In single-player the train's physics was doing more work each tick than the ride needed, and on a long train it dragged the whole game behind you: blocks you had mined broke late, hits landed late, and mobs moved as if underwater. The train now runs lighter, so what you do happens when you do it.

- Blocks break and drop the moment you finish mining them.
- Hits, knockback and mob movement keep up with you.

### 0.921.0

**Test the Carriage no longer freezes low-end PCs on the way in or out**

Entering or leaving Test the Carriage with Skybox Blocks switched off used to rebuild every chunk in view at once — on a low-end PC that was a long stall going in and a hard freeze coming back. Now only the chunks that actually hold a Skybox Block are redrawn, so the test starts and ends as quickly as the teleport itself. The room's fog and daylight also stopped flickering on and off during a test.

- Only Skybox Block chunks are redrawn when a test starts or ends, not the whole view
- Dimensional-carriage fog and sky no longer switch on and off every tick while you test

### 0.920.0

**Beds aboard the train stop exploding after the Nether**

A bed placed inside a carriage that had rolled through the Nether could still blow up long after the train was back in the overworld. Beds on board now behave like the world outside the window: safe in the overworld, still deadly while the train is inside the Nether or the End.

### 0.919.0

**Entering the plot you are already in keeps your edits — from the track roof too**

Stepping back into the plot you are standing in is a walk to its menu, not a reload. Every plot now agrees on that, and the track tile is no exception: Go here or Enter from its roof no longer wipes what you built.

- Go here / Enter from inside any plot keeps unsaved edits, track tile roof included.
- Dimensional carriage names typed in any case land in the right room.

### 0.918.0

**Beds no longer claim to set a respawn point**

Sleeping in a bed on the train used to answer with 'Respawn point set — aboard the train' and similar lines, which read as if the bed worked like a normal spawn. Every bed message now says plainly that no respawn point was set — the train is your only way back, wherever it has rolled. All 20 languages carry the corrected wording.

### 0.917.0

**Every editor lands you the same way**

Where you arrive when you enter a plot — on the roof facing its menu, in its front doorway, or at its centre — used to be worked out separately by each of the seven editors. It is now decided in one place, so carriages, dimensional carriages, parts, pillars, tracks and tunnels can never drift apart. Nothing moves for you: every landing is exactly where it was.

- One landing rule shared by all seven editors, covered by tests for each way in.
- A plot with no doorway simply lands you at its centre — no special cases per editor.

### 0.916.0

**Pictures stay on the wall for good**

The fix that stopped Fast Paintings pictures dropping off the wall whenever a build, plot or carriage was loaded now lives in one place instead of twelve, and a build-time check makes sure no future loader can bring the bug back.

- One named setting owns how every template is stamped into the world, with the reason written down once.
- A test fails the build if any loader ever reaches for the old setting that popped pictures.

### 0.915.0

**The rest of the editor commands confirm in chat again**

The same 0.908.0 regression that silenced the editor enter lines also hit a further fourteen editor messages — setting a carriage, track or contents weight, flipping contents, baking a stage palette, replacing a block across a stage, the part-plot enter line, the "target block is outside the plot" warnings, and the portal-carriage save confirmation. All of them now reach chat instead of failing into the log.

- Weight, flip, stage bake and stage replaceblock commands report their result and the file they wrote
- Every remaining message the mod prints is now checked by a build-time test so this class of bug cannot ship again

### 0.914.0

**Loading a build shows it, even from inside the plot**

Loading a build from the relay while standing in its plot now brings the new blocks in with you. Before, the plot kept showing what was there already, and saving would quietly write that back over the build you had just loaded.

- Load and Replace refresh the plot you are standing in.
- Go here and the panel's Enter still keep your unsaved edits.

### 0.912.0

**Outdated clients are turned away at login instead of being kicked mid-session**

Joining a server with a Dungeon Train build older than the server's could work at first and then drop you the moment you used a plot panel in the editor, because the two builds disagreed about what that message looked like. The network version now says so up front: a mismatched client sees the usual mod-mismatch screen at login, with both versions listed, and a matching one joins as before. A check in the build pipeline keeps this from slipping again.

- Client and server builds that disagree are refused at login, not dropped mid-game
- The mismatch screen names both versions so you know which side to update

**Editor plots enter cleanly again**

Entering any editor plot — a carriage, tunnel, pillar, contents or track plot — or creating a new one printed a red "enter failed" error in chat even though you had arrived. The green "entered … plot at x, y, z" line is back and the error is gone.

- Affects every editor enter and new/clone command since v0.907.

### 0.911.0

**Editor: relay Load result lands on the right build**

Loading a build from the X menu while clicking other tiles no longer credits the result to the wrong one.

**Entering a built-up plot no longer stalls the server**

Pressing Enter on a plot whose doorway and door row are blocked — a raised floor, a wall across the door, a pillar in the centre — used to freeze the game for a moment on large rooms while it looked for somewhere to put you. It now finds the nearest free spot straight away, and you land in exactly the same place as before.

- Enter on a 64×64×64 room with a raised floor is instant instead of dropping a few ticks
- Landing spot is unchanged — still the nearest free cell inside, never in the wall

### 0.910.0

**Backrooms carriage re-saved in current editor format**

The Backrooms dimensional carriage's variant data was re-saved from the editor in the current format. Nothing changes in-game.

**Editor: place mobs like blocks**

A new Settings row, Mobs | Blocks | Live (default Blocks), changes what a spawn egg does in an editor plot. Under Blocks the mob stands frozen on the cell you clicked, facing you, and one hit removes it — so you can place and clear mobs the way you place blocks, and they stay where you put them until you save. **Block-variant cells show a ghost cube instead of a command block**

**Save-as keeps a template's block variants**

Saving a bundled carriage, interior or part under a new name in the editor no longer drops its block variants — the new copy keeps every variant cell the original had.

- Contents, carriage and part editors all carry variants across a save-as

**Your Ender Chest survives a crash**

If the game crashed, your Ender Chest used to come back as it was at the end of the previous session — everything you had put in during the crashed one was gone. It now keeps whatever was in it at the last autosave, so a crash costs you at most a few minutes, the same as the rest of your inventory. Ender Chest Persistence 0.5.0 is now required; the CurseForge and Modrinth apps update it for you.

- Ender Chest contents are saved every autosave and whenever you switch game mode, not only when you leave the world

In the editor, a variant clipboard now works with Effortless Building's shape modes. Pick Floor, Wall or Cube with the clipboard in hand and every cell of the shape gets the copied variant pool in one go — lock group, copy settings and any container loot included — instead of one cell per click. One Ctrl+Z undoes the whole paste.

- Floor / Wall / Cube (and the mirror, array and radial modifiers) all work with a variant clipboard
- A plain right-click still pastes a single cell

The CurseForge and Modrinth apps install both mods for you; if you install by hand, grab Fast Paintings and Moonlight for NeoForge 1.21.1.

- Saved builds and shared carriages keep every painting, size and picture included
- Mirrored carriage interiors keep their paintings; they re-hang on the opposite wall instead of dropping
- Two new required mods, Fast Paintings and Moonlight — auto-installed by the CurseForge and Modrinth apps
